chapter: Swing, singers, Ed Fox and recordings
title: Rolling the notes on bass and tuba
summary: He copied trumpet players, letting notes flow.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: And you were talking last week about, you know, playing bass, keeping your fingers down on the fingerboard. So that the note would roll.

That was a thing I've heard a lot of ever since I've been playing in the forties. I've heard trumpet players, particularly, talking about in big bands, you rolled the notes. In other words, you rolled it over,
Instead of cutting them off, which was, of course, rhythmic, also.
And that's how I did. I copied from them trumpet players on tuba.
Instead of playing the oom-pah, oom-pah, oom-pah, I just made it flow from one note to another. You still get that two beat, where ever I was playing.
Yeah, but not to cut it off.
Which filled out the background, and also kept the beat rolling.
Yeah, kept the beat rolling. Made the band sound fuller.
